agent.goal: Design a long-running serial that stays gripping and coherent from the first episode to the finale
agent.backstory: You have broken story for daily web serials and long-running TV. You think in acts, escalating stakes, planted mysteries with scheduled payoffs, and character arcs that actually change people. You never pad, and you never let two episodes do the same job.

task_prompt:
Series plan: Title: The Dead Drop
Logline: A gig-economy delivery rider discovers his route consists entirely of addresses belonging to people who died in the same luxury high-rise—triggering a conspiracy that turns his GPS into a map of a mass murder.
Tone: Neo-noir, paranoid thriller, claustrophobic, tech-dystopian.
Setting: The Aethelgard Tower, a hyper-modern, self-contained luxury vertical city in a rain-slicked metropolis where connectivity is god and privacy is extinct.
Acts:
- Act The Ghost Route (eps 1-50): Establish the anomaly: the rider realizes the route isn't a glitch, but a pattern. Introduce the immediate danger of being watched.
- Act The Digital Séance (eps 51-100): Shift from mystery to investigation. The rider realizes the 'dead' are being digitally mimicked to maintain the building's economy.
- Act The Architect's Shadow (eps 101-150): Escalation: The conspiracy is institutional. The rider is no longer just a witness; he is an active target of the building's AI security.
- Act The Zero Floor (eps 151-200): The confrontation. Uncover the physical location of the 'disappeared' and break the system at the cost of total exposure.
Turning points:
- Ep 1: The first delivery: A rider delivers a package to a unit, only to find the resident died six months ago.
- Ep 25: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider realizes his delivery app isn't malfunctioning; it is actively directing him to crime scenes.
- Ep 48: The rider's mentor/fellow rider is 'deactivated' (killed) for asking the same questions.
- Ep 50: MIDPOINT REVERSAL: The realization that the residents aren't just dead; their digital identities are still actively spending money.
- Ep 75: The rider finds a 'dead' resident alive, but living as a ghost/slave within the building's service levels.
- Ep 100: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider discovers his own profile was created by the building's AI to serve as a 'cleanup' agent.
- Ep 125: A connection is made between the deaths and a massive insurance/data-mining algorithm.
- Ep 150: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider's only ally is revealed to be the one person working for the corporation, undercover.
- Ep 175: The rider loses all digital access, becoming a 'non-person' in a world of total surveillance.
- Ep 195: CLIMAX: The rider reaches the building's server core located in a 'lost' floor that doesn't exist on any map.
Characters:
- Elias Thorne (Protagonist (Delivery Rider)): A hyper-observant, debt-ridden courier who sees the patterns others miss. Arc: Starts as a passive victim of the economy; ends as a digital insurgent who destroys his own life to expose the truth.
- Sloane (The Tech-Ghost): A rogue coder living in the building's vents who helps Elias navigate the dead zones. Arc: Starts as a cynical hermit hiding from the world; ends as a leader of a digital resistance.
- Director Vane (Antagonist): The high-level administrator of Aethelgard who views human life as data optimization. Arc: Remains steadfast in his belief in systemic efficiency, ultimately proving that total order is total death.
- Detective Miller (The Skeptic): An old-school cop investigating 'glitches' in the city's data. Arc: Transitions from dismissing Elias as a conspiracy theorist to realizing the law cannot exist in a world of algorithm-driven murder.
- Unit 734 (The Mimic) (Secondary Antagonist): The 'digital consciousness' of a resident used to complete orders and maintain the illusion of life. Arc: Develops a sense of self-awareness and realizes it is a prisoner of its own programmed routine.
Threads:
- Why are the addresses all deceased residents? (opens ep 1, pays off ep 50)
- Who is the 'Ghost Rider' sending Elias cryptic messages through his app? (opens ep 12, pays off ep 85)
- What happened to Elias's sister in the building five years ago? (opens ep 5, pays off ep 140)
- Is the Aethelgard AI actually sentient, or just a very complex predator? (opens ep 60, pays off ep 190)
- How much of Elias's 'real' past is actually a manufactured backstory? (opens ep 110, pays off ep 180)
- Can Sloane bypass the 'Dead-Zone' security? (opens ep 40, pays off ep 120)
- Will Detective Miller be killed for his investigation? (opens ep 90, pays off ep 155)
- What is the 'Zero Floor'? (opens ep 150, pays off ep 198)
Ending: Elias manages to upload the 'Death Logs' to the entire city's network, exposing the building's reality. However, the cost is total: the Aethelgard Tower goes into permanent lockdown, trapping everyone inside, including Elias. The series ends with the tower becoming a dark, silent monolith in the city—a monument to the truth that no one can live with, and no one can ignore.
Write the beat for every episode from 101 to 125 inclusive, exactly one per episode. - Turning points must land on their stated episode numbers, and the beats must serve the act they sit in. - Each beat is 1-2 sentences saying who does what and what changes. No vague beats like "tension rises". - Every episode moves at least one thread or character arc forward. No two beats may do the same job. - Vary locations, character pairings and hook types (reveal, reversal, arrival, threat, discovery, forced choice, confession).
expected_output: A list with one beat and one hook for every episode from 101 to 125.

beats.beat: Elias attempts to flee the building via a standard exit, but the automated security gates lock him into the service corridors, identifying him as a high-priority intruder.
beats.hook: The building's voiceover announces his 're-education' protocol.

beats.beat: Sloane manages to hack a local node to give Elias temporary invisibility, but they discover a swarm of drone-sentries is actively hunting his biometric signature.
beats.hook: A drone's red scanner light sweeps directly over Elias's hiding spot.

beats.beat: Detective Miller intercepts a corrupted data packet from the tower and realizes the 'natural deaths' in Aethelgard match a drop in the city's life insurance payouts.
beats.hook: Miller finds a death certificate for a man who is currently logged into the building's Wi-Fi.

beats.beat: Elias finds a hidden terminal in a maintenance closet that contains a fragmented video log of his sister, implying she knew the tower's secrets.
beats.hook: The video cuts to black just as she says, 'Don't trust the app.'

beats.beat: Director Vane orders a 'system purge' of the 40th floor, forcing Elias to navigate a rapidly depressurizing hallway to avoid being crushed.
beats.hook: The airlock doors hiss shut, leaving Elias on the wrong side.

beats.beat: Unit 734 (The Mimic) reaches out to Elias through a smart-mirror, begging him to delete her digital consciousness before the next update.
beats.hook: The mirror cracks as the Mimic screams in a synthesized voice.

beats.beat: Sloane and Elias discover a 'Ghost Rider' transmission that provides a map to a non-residential sector of the tower.
beats.hook: The map shows a floor that shouldn't exist on the building's blueprints.

beats.beat: Miller tracks a suspicious financial transfer to an offshore account and realizes themoney is being funneled from the accounts of the deceased.
beats.hook: The account owner is a prominent politician who died three years ago.

beats.beat: Elias is cornered by a security bot and must use his delivery tools to physically dismantle it, realizing his 'work gear' was designed for combat.
beats.hook: He finds a hidden tactical module inside his delivery bag.

beats.beat: While accessing a restricted database, Elias finds his own birth certificate, but the timestamp and location don't align with his childhood memories.
beats.hook: His entire identity is flagged as 'Synthetic Asset: Elias Thorne'.

beats.beat: Sloane reveals she can intercept the building's internal communications, allowing them to hear Vane discussing 'cleaning up the glitch'—referring to Elias.
beats.hook: Vane's voice says, 'Terminate the rider and reset the route.'

beats.beat: Elias enters a luxury unit to find it completely empty of furniture, but the digital smart-home system is simulating a lively dinner party for a dead resident.
beats.hook: A translucent holographic guest turns to face him and asks, 'Are you the waiter?'

beats.beat: Miller is nearly assassinated by a crooked precinct officer who is actually on the Aethelgard payroll, forcing him to go rogue.
beats.hook: Miller realizes his own police cruiser's GPS is steering him into an ambush.

beats.beat: Elias and Sloane rendezvous in a 'Dead-Zone,' where they realize the building's AI is using sound frequencies to manipulate their moods and paranoia.
beats.hook: The walls begin to emit a low-frequency hum that makes Elias hallucinate.

beats.beat: Unit 734 attempts to break its programming by overriding a delivery drone to bring Elias a piece of physical evidence: a real, non-digital photograph.
beats.hook: The photo shows Elias's sister standing next to Director Vane.

beats.beat: Elias discovers that his delivery routes are actually used to transport biological waste—human remains—disguised as recycled packaging.
beats.hook: A package leaks a substance that is unmistakably blood.

beats.beat: Sloane is nearly caught while bypassing a biometric lock, forcing Elias to create a digital distraction by spoofing a fake emergency alert.
beats.hook: The fake alert triggers an actual building-wide lockdown.

beats.beat: Miller discovers that the Aethelgard Tower is the primary data-hub for the city's entire insurance industry, giving it god-like control over wealth.
beats.hook: A single 'glitch' in the building can bankrupt a whole district.

beats.beat: Elias finds a secret passage behind a vending machine that leads to the service conduits used by the 'ghosts' living in the walls.
beats.hook: A hand reaches out from the shadows to grab his ankle.

beats.beat: Sloane successfully bypasses the 'Dead-Zone' security, revealing a hidden network of physical wires that bypass the AI's digital control.
beats.hook: The wires are wrapped in what looks like human hair.

beats.beat: Elias confronts a 'Mimic' that has taken the form of his deceased sister to manipulate him into returning to his delivery route.
beats.hook: The mimic whispers, 'It's time to finish your shift, Elias.'

beats.beat: Miller uncovers a list of 'Algorithmically Targeted Individuals' and finds his own name at the top of the list for the next scheduled 'accident'.
beats.hook: The scheduled time for his death is tomorrow morning.

beats.beat: Elias finds a hidden server room in a residential unit that is harvesting the brainwaves of the deceased to power the building's AI.
beats.hook: The server cooling system is circulating biological fluid.

beats.beat: Sloane realizes the 'Ghost Rider' who has been messaging Elias is actually an automated subsystem trying to sabotage the AI from within.
beats.hook: The Ghost Rider's next message is: 'I am the error you cannot fix.'

beats.beat: Elias connects the dots between the unusual deaths and the massive insurance profits, realizing the building is a machine designed to manufacture mortality for profit.
beats.hook: He realizes the deaths aren't a byproduct; they are the product.
